newsitem.title: USA: Unclear how much CPI overstates inflation - Rivlin.
newsitem.headline: Unclear how much CPI overstates inflation - Rivlin.

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin said on Wednesday that the U.S. Consumer Price Index clearly overstated inflation, but noted that the size of the overstatement was unclear.

"Clearly the consumer price index as currently structured does overstate inflation somewhat although how much is a little bit unclear," she said, speaking at a dinner ahead of the Senior Executives' Conference of the Mortgage Bankers Association of America.
She suggested giving the Bureau of Labour Statistics the resources to improve the index over several years.

In the meantime, she said "one might take a very conservative estimate of the overestimate ... maybe it's a half a percent ... and we might reduce our indexing presumably both of social security and taxes by a half a percent ... until the BLS is able to improve the index."
Rivlin also came out against the idea of investing Social Security money in the stock market, as some members of a recent commission on Social Security reform suggested.
"Its only attractivenes is that it appears to give you more revenue into the Social Security trust fund," Rivlin said.
"It seems to me ... that it's not a very good idea. Do we want the government owning common stocks or bonds? ... It's not a position that we've historically wanted our government in," she said.
